subject.title: fix: stabilize embedded prompt caching across policy and Responses boundaries

question: Should non-owner and ambient turns receive stable model-visible schemas for protected core tools while execution is denied immediately before hooks and side effects?
rationale: The code and tests can prove enforcement, but they cannot decide whether prompt-cache stability justifies exposing protected tool names and schemas to unauthorized turns.

options.title: Keep stable schemas with runtime denial
options.body: Accept stable protected-tool visibility and require exact refreshed-head proof that every denied call fails before hooks and side effects.

options.title: Hide protected schemas
options.body: Retain the least-visible inventory even though sender and room-event transitions can invalidate the reusable prompt prefix.

options.title: Split the boundary change
options.body: Land lower-risk continuation and propagation repairs separately while reviewing protected-schema visibility in a narrower PR.

recommendation.title: Keep stable schemas with runtime denial
recommendation.body: Accept stable protected-tool visibility and require exact refreshed-head proof that every denied call fails before hooks and side effects.

likelyOwner.reason: The central affected runtime surfaces and consolidated current-main ownership history make him the strongest available decision router.
